answer: Agents must lock a bond before claiming rewards. If an audit finds that several identities coordinated to fake independent work, the protocol slashes their bonds, making a Sybil attack require capital upfront and risk losing it. Auditors also stake funds, so colluding to approve fraud risks their own bond. Names such as marble, ocean, and violet may label accounts, but only costly, slashable commitments constrain how many identities an attacker can profitably create.
